intro_text: A Sinai resort with the best diving in Egypt: a visa on arrival (simplified entry within Sinai), a warm sea and well-developed tourist infrastructure. The downsides are its isolation from a big city and the summer heat.
pros: Simplified Sinai entry and a visa on arrival
The best diving and coral reefs in Egypt
A warm sea and sunshine almost year-round

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.answer: Simplified entry applies to the Sinai coast; for travel further afield you need a visa on arrival.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.answer: Affordable out of season, more expensive in tourist areas. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.answer: Arabic; English and Russian are widely used in tourism.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You need cash pounds and a foreign bank card.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.answer: Coastal desert: hot summers and warm, mild winters.

faq.question: How does Sharm differ from Hurghada?
faq.answer: Sharm has better diving and reefs and is more isolated; Hurghada is larger and closer to a big city.

reviews.text: Sharm means world-class reefs and a warm sea in winter. The downside is the isolation: there's little infrastructure beyond the resort, and the summers are very hot.
I wintered in Naama Bay: sun, diving, a Russian-speaking environment. Prices in tourist spots bite, but out of season living is quite affordable.
